column1: Authentication: Ensures that only legitimate users, devices, and network entities can access services.

column3: Ensures that only authorized users can access the network
Verifies the legitimacy of network nodes (eNodeB, gNodeB, AMF, SMF, etc.)
Guarantees two-way authentication between UE and the network to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks
Enforces token-based authentication between SBA functions
Protects against forced redirection to rogue or unauthorized PLMNs
Ensures consistent authentication policies across operators during roaming

column1: Authorization: Controls permissions and restricts operations to authorized entities only.

column3: Enforces strict authorization for APIs and service-based interfaces
Prevents unauthorized modification of policies, QoS, or charging rules
Ensures strong isolation between MEC applications
Requires strong authorization and input validation for SBA REST APIs
Ensures strict separation between 5G network slices (eMBB, URLLC, mMTC, etc.)
Guarantees tenant isolation in SBA and MEC environments
Enforces logical separation between core network functions (AMF, SMF, UPF, etc.)

column1: Service Integrity: Guarantees that services, signaling, and data remain correct, unaltered, and trustworthy.

column3: Ensures signaling and data messages are not altered during transmission
Ensures NAS/RRC security contexts are established before sensitive exchanges
Validates paging messages and prevents spoofed triggers
Ensures integrity-protected emergency registration and deregistration

column1: Service Confidentiality: Protects sensitive signaling and user data from unauthorized access or disclosure.

column3: Protects user data and signaling from interception
Ensures sensitive information remains protected at all times
Ensures both encryption and integrity protections are activated together
Prevents downgrades to weak ciphering or integrity algorithms
Secures key re-derivation and renewal during mobility or context switches
Ensures secure generation, distribution, update, and revocation of cryptographic keys

column1: Privacy Protection: Prevents leakage of sensitive identifiers, location information, and other personal data.

column3: Ensures SUPI, SUCI, GUTI, and other permanent identifiers are never exposed in plaintext
Protects against tracking through paging, TA updates, or broadcast messages
Prevents identity leakage during paging in multi-network environments
Ensures slice, subscription, and policy data remain confidential

column1: Network Availability & Signaling Security: Ensures the continuous availability and reliability of network services by protecting against attacks that disrupt connectivity or signaling procedures.

column3: Protects against resource exhaustion attacks
Detects and mitigates signaling flood attacks
Identifies and blocks connections to fake eNodeBs/gNodeBs
Defends against RF jamming, replay, and signal spoofing attacks

column1: Interworking Security: Ensures secure and consistent behavior when UEs operate across different access technologies, network generations, and specification layers.

column3: Blocks fallback to insecure or legacy specifications
Prevents vulnerabilities caused by NAS, RRC, SBA, and IP interactions
Ensures secure, consistent behavior across 4G, 5G, NSA, and SA deployments

column1: Threat Detection & Logging: Enables real-time anomaly detection.

column3: Monitors interactions across NAS, RRC, SBA, and user-plane layers
Maintains secure, tamper-proof logs
Validates specification timers to prevent exploitation
Ensure NAS/RRC/PDCP counters are strictly monotonic, unique, and correctly synchronized between UE and network. Detect and prevent counter wrap-around, reuse, or desynchronization.

column1: Regulatory Compliance: Ensures compliance with regulations and protects against fraud.

column3: Enforces lawful intercept, data protection, and privacy regulations
Prevents manipulation of charging data and unauthorized resource usage
